component.name: Gear Lever COSMIC
component.summary: Add AppImages to your app menu and keep them updated

description.p: Add AppImages to your app menu, keep them updated, and see clearly what can and cannot be updated. Inspired by Gear Lever and rewritten in Rust with libcosmic.

Updates replace the file in place, so running apps keep working and switch to the new version when they restart. Versions are read from the AppImage itself, menu entries are refreshed when an app updated itself, and apps with their own updater are labelled as such. It also checks whether an AppImage can start on this system (FUSE 2 or FUSE 3, missing libraries).
A command line tool with typed commands, dry-run plans and live window controls makes everything usable by scripts and AI agents.

Dragging AppImages onto the window now works on X11 desktops (such as Thunar on XFCE) as well as Wayland, showing the drop banner and opening dropped files on the Add page. The window now also sets its X11 icon and window class so the Gear Lever COSMIC logo appears in X11 taskbars, panels, and window switchers.

The AppImage now opens on X11 desktops (such as XFCE, Cinnamon, MATE, and X11 sessions on openSUSE Leap, Debian, Fedora, and Ubuntu) instead of crashing on startup when the system's libxkbcommon version differs from the build container's. It bundles matching X11, XCB, libxkbcommon-x11, and Wayland client libraries alongside its bundled libxkbcommon while continuing to load host GPU drivers through cross-libc-dlopen.

The AppImage now uses the host's Vulkan GPU driver on distributions whose Vulkan ICD manifests list a bare library file name instead of a full path (such as Arch Linux, CachyOS, and several NVIDIA driver packages) even when the host glibc is newer than the AppImage's bundled glibc. Previously those drivers failed to load and the window fell back to software rendering, making scrolling choppy. The AppImage startup hook resolves bare ICD names to absolute host paths for its own process, respects any user-set VK_DRIVER_FILES or VK_ICD_FILENAMES, skips CLI runs, and strips its generated VK_DRIVER_FILES from apps launched by Gear Lever COSMIC.

Adding an AppImage that is already in the AppImages folder under its standard name, such as one whose app deleted its own menu entry, now writes a menu entry for that file where it is instead of making a second copy next to it.

A running app's page now has a Quit button. It lists the processes it will stop, including background helpers an app leaves running after its window closes (which kept such apps shown as running), and asks them to quit as at logout. Anything still running after 10 seconds can be force quit, which stops it at once and loses unsaved work. Quit is not available in the Flatpak.

Remove and Force Quit buttons are red. The update progress bar spans the whole banner, and the Update All result is shorter: one line per app with its old and new version, each note once, and an Open Report button. While updates install and after they finish, the Updates page says so instead of reporting that no updates were found, and Update All is hidden when nothing is ready. The AppImage now carries a small metadata image in front of its DwarFS filesystem, so tools that read only SquashFS can show its name and icon.

DwarFS AppImages that carry a small SquashFS metadata image in front of the application (written by appimagetool with SQUASHFS_METADATA_SIDECAR=1 and skipped by uruntime 0.8.3) are read correctly: the application's own filesystem is read, not just the metadata image, so system requirement checks find the program again. Built with Rust 1.100.0, the latest libcosmic and crates, and the newest Anylinux tooling (quick-sharun with appimagetool 0.7.0 and sharun 3.9.0, uruntime 0.8.3 with DwarFS 0.15.8).

Gear Lever COSMIC now also ships as a 64-bit ARM AppImage (GearLever_COSMIC-VERSION-aarch64.AppImage), tested on Apple Silicon Macs running Asahi Linux with 16 KB memory pages; each AppImage updates only to the build for its own architecture. When a release offers files for several architectures, ARM computers now pick the 64-bit ARM file instead of any ARM file, and an update whose file is built for a different architecture than the installed one is refused before anything is replaced.

Updates never offer a file built for another architecture: apps that update themselves through electron-updater are checked against their own architecture's feed (an up-to-date ARM app no longer shows "Update available" forever), FTP sources pick the file for the installed architecture from the newest version folder and work with servers that refuse SIZE in text mode, and a release with no file for it is reported as not found instead of available. When several apps are updated at once and one fails, the others are still updated, and every result is shown. x86_64 AppImages run through qemu on ARM computers are recognised as running, including after an update, and can be relaunched. Forgejo and GitLab addresses with a port work, the published .sha256 files verify with sha256sum -c, and parallel operations no longer fail as "Another operation is running" when a program starts at the same moment.

No more false "Menu outdated" badges: menu entries no longer carry a version, versions are read from the AppImage files, and the menu-outdated check and its "Keep menu entries in sync" setting are gone. The app page's Reload still rewrites a menu entry from its file. File fingerprints no longer include the device number, which btrfs can change across reboots and which made every app look changed. An app that still runs a version an update replaced can be restarted with Relaunch on its page or in the update result: it is asked to quit as at logout and started from the new file, and is never force-closed. The window no longer crashes when no AppImages are installed yet, and every icon it uses is bundled, so it needs no icon theme from the desktop.

The remove, update and set-update-source commands accept an app by id or name, as the other commands do, instead of only a file path; an unknown app now lists the known ids rather than reporting an integrated app as not integrated. The agent guide and bundled docs show the command that really starts the CLI instead of a made-up AppImage file name. The CLI can be put on PATH as gearlever-cosmic-cli (cli.link, a Settings switch, and automatically when Gear Lever COSMIC adds itself to the app menu), and apps that are also installed as a Flatpak are flagged, since the app menu then shows them twice.

AppImages whose file name still carries a version (such as App-1.2-x86_64.appimage) can be given their standard name with one click ("Use Standard Name") or app.rename-file, together with their menu entry and icon, even while they run. Help, guide and docs now show the command that actually starts the CLI, such as the AppImage's full path followed by cli. Apps started with Launch no longer hang: their output goes to a log file (~/.local/share/gearlever-cosmic/launch-logs) instead of a pipe that closed once the launcher returned, which stopped Electron apps such as ZCode from loading. The AppImage no longer bundles unrelated system data, and it can be built on any common Linux distribution.

Faster and lighter: command-line output can be captured in 0.2 s instead of 6 s, the window uses about 40% less memory than before, AppImages built with current DwarFS tools (including this one) are read correctly, and refreshing a menu entry restores missing details such as the window icon match.

First release: Gear Lever's features in a native COSMIC app, in-place updates of running apps, honest update statuses, versions read from the file (Gear Lever issue #497), system requirement checks, custom icons that survive updates, and an agent CLI.
